lead: Interchangeable parts need agreed sizes. Preferred numbers fix the standard sizes and ratings (shaft diameters, motor powers, press capacities) so that factories make a few well-chosen variants instead of hundreds. Fits and tolerances fix how much a size may vary and how a shaft sits in its hole, with a planned clearance or grip. A 25 mm shaft made in Coimbatore must enter a 25 mm hole bored in Pune. This chapter gives the series, the vocabulary, the ISO code such as H7/g6 and how its limits are calculated.

blocks.text: Preferred numbers, first proposed by Charles Renard and standardised as ISO 3, are geometric series: each term is the previous one times a fixed ratio. The basic series are R5, R10, R20 and R40, with 5, 10, 20 and 40 terms in each decade (1 to 10, 10 to 100, and so on).
q = ¹⁰√10 for R10; in general q = 101/n, and the terms are 10i/n rounded

head: Series
Rounded terms in the decade 10 to 100

blocks.text: Geometric spacing gives equal relative steps: about 26 % between R10 terms whether the size is 10 mm or 100 mm. Small sizes get fine choices, large sizes coarse ones, and each coarser series is part of the finer one, so R5 sizes are also R10 sizes. A derived series takes every p-th term of a basic series: R10/3 takes every third term of R10, giving 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (ratio about 2). A 25 mm shaft is a preferred size; 24.8 mm is not.

sections.h3: Basic size, limits, tolerance and deviation

blocks.text: The basic size D is the size named on the drawing, 25 mm in the example. No machinist can hit D exactly at an affordable cost, so the drawing gives an upper limit and a lower limit, the largest and smallest acceptable sizes.
The tolerance is the full permitted band, in mm or μm (1 μm = 0.001 mm). A size 25 ± 0.010 mm has limits 25.010 and 24.990 mm and a tolerance of 0.020 mm, not 0.010 mm.

A deviation is a limit minus the basic size, with its sign. For a hole the upper and lower deviations are written ES and EI; for a shaft, es and ei (capitals for holes, small letters for shafts). The fundamental deviation is the one nearer the basic size; its letter (H, g, p…) places the tolerance zone, and the IT grade number (IT01 to IT18) sets the width of the zone. A smaller IT number is a tighter tolerance.

i is the standard tolerance unit in μm; D (mm) is the geometric mean of the diameter step that contains the basic size (for 18 to 30 mm, D = √(18 × 30) = 23.24 mm). For the shaft letters the standard gives fundamental deviations such as es = −2.5D<sup>0.34</sup> μm for g and es = −5.5D<sup>0.41</sup> μm for f; letter h has es = 0 and hole H has EI = 0.

A fit is the relation between a hole and the shaft in it. In a clearance fit the smallest hole is never smaller than the largest shaft, so the clearance is never negative (H7/h6 has a minimum clearance of exactly zero). In an interference fit the smallest shaft is always larger than the largest hole, so the parts must be pressed or shrunk together. In a transition fit the zones overlap and one pair may have a small clearance and the next a small interference.

Allowance is the planned difference at the tightest assembly: smallest hole minus largest shaft. It is the minimum clearance, or (if negative) the maximum interference. Clearance itself is the actual gap in one assembled pair and lies between the minimum and maximum clearance.

In the hole-basis system every hole is H (EI = 0, so the smallest hole is the basic size) and the shaft letter sets the fit; it is preferred because a few standard reamers and plug gauges make every hole. In the shaft-basis system every shaft is h (es = 0) and the hole letter is varied; it suits long bright bars with many parts on them. A fit is always written hole first: H7/g6 is hole-basis, G7/h6 is shaft-basis.

blocks.text: Bearing and gear seatings are chosen from the manufacturers' tables; see the chapters on rolling contact bearings and gears. In a chain of parts the worst-case tolerance of the gap is the sum of the part tolerances: five parts of 0.020 mm give 0.100 mm.

examples.question: A firm makes six sizes of hydraulic press from 10 kN to 100 kN. Find the capacities from a preferred-number series.
steps: Six sizes from 10 to 100 kN means five equal ratio steps: q⁵ = 100/10 = 10, so q = 10<sup>1/5</sup> = 1.585. This is the R5 ratio.
Round to the R5 values: 10, 16, 25, 40, 63, 100 kN.

examples.question: Calculate the limits of the fit 25 H7/g6. The diameter step is 18 to 30 mm; use i = 0.45∛D + 0.001D, IT7 = 16i, IT6 = 10i and, for g, es = −2.5D<sup>0.34</sup> (all in μm). Find the maximum and minimum clearance and name the type of fit.
steps: Geometric mean of the step: D = √(18 × 30) = 23.24 mm.
Hole tolerance IT7 = 16 × 1.307 = 20.9 ≈ 21 μm. Shaft tolerance IT6 = 10 × 1.307 = 13.1 ≈ 13 μm.
Hole H: EI = 0, ES = +21 μm. Limits 25.000 mm and 25.021 mm.
Maximum clearance = largest hole − smallest shaft = 25.021 − 24.980 = 0.041 mm. Minimum clearance (the allowance) = smallest hole − largest shaft = 25.000 − 24.993 = 0.007 mm.
examples.answer: Hole 25.000/25.021 mm, shaft 24.980/24.993 mm; clearance from 0.007 mm to 0.041 mm, so 25 H7/g6 is a clearance fit (hole-basis), with hole tolerance 0.021 mm and shaft tolerance 0.013 mm.

traps: Tolerance is the full band, not the ± value: 25 ± 0.010 mm has a tolerance of 0.020 mm.
Writing the shaft first. ISO always writes the hole first: H7/g6, G7/h6. A capital letter is always the hole.
Minimum clearance uses the smallest hole and the largest shaft; maximum clearance the largest hole and the smallest shaft. Swapping them gives a wrong sign.
Using the basic size itself as D in the tolerance-unit formula. D is the geometric mean of the step (23.24 mm for 18 to 30 mm).
Calling H7/h6 a transition fit because its minimum clearance is zero. It is a clearance fit.

quiz.q: What does R10 mean, and what is its ratio?
quiz.a: A geometric series of preferred numbers with 10 terms per decade; ratio 10<sup>1/10</sup> = 1.259.

quiz.q: Name the three classes of fit.
Why are preferred numbers geometric rather than arithmetic?
quiz.a: Geometric steps give the same relative change at every size, so small parts get small steps and large parts large ones, and one series covers a wide range with few sizes.

quiz.q: Why is the hole-basis system preferred in most workshops?
quiz.a: Holes are made with fixed-size tools (drills, reamers) and checked with plug gauges. Keeping every hole H means one set of tools and gauges per size; the shaft, turned or ground on a lathe, is easily made to any size.

quiz.q: A 40 mm hole has limits 40.000 and 40.025 mm and the shaft 39.975 and 39.991 mm. Find the maximum and minimum clearance and the fit type.
quiz.a: Maximum clearance 40.025 − 39.975 = 0.050 mm; minimum clearance 40.000 − 39.991 = 0.009 mm. Both positive: a clearance fit (it is 40 H7/g6).

quiz.q: For 50 H7/p6 the hole is 50.000/50.025 mm and the shaft 50.026/50.042 mm. Find the maximum and minimum interference.
quiz.a: Maximum interference = largest shaft − smallest hole = 50.042 − 50.000 = 0.042 mm. Minimum interference = smallest shaft − largest hole = 50.026 − 50.025 = 0.001 mm. An interference fit.

quiz.q: A drawing changes a hub fit from H7/g6 to H7/p6 at the same size. What changes on the shop floor and in service?
quiz.a: The parts no longer slide together: assembly needs a press or heating of the hub; the hub carries hoop stress; the joint transmits some torque by friction; removal may damage the surfaces.

beyond: Real drawings add geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T: flatness, position, runout) to size limits, and tolerance analysis software runs Monte Carlo stacks on whole assemblies. The ISO 286 tables replace the formulas of this chapter in daily work, and the design data book gives them for every step and grade. Search next for ISO 286 limits and fits tables, GD&T position tolerance and tolerance stack-up analysis.

figure.caption: Tolerance zones at 25 mm drawn to scale about the zero line (the basic size). The H7 hole runs from 0 to +21 μm; with a g6 shaft the zones never overlap, so the fit always has clearance (0.007 to 0.041 mm, as in the second worked example); a k6 shaft overlaps the hole zone (transition) and a p6 shaft lies wholly above it (interference).
